note: Root-family split of a certified corpus; nothing was synthesized. v2 supersedes openui_verified_train_v1, which was untrainable: 29 of its 1,083 admitted records placed a placeholder in a non-content property and TwoTowerModel.from_records refused the first one, taking every screening arm down with it. v1 is immutable and stays as built; admission is now stricter and v2 is the rebuild. Each recommendation names an admission-time action the build performs, verified by re-measuring the admitted records rather than asserting it. Receipts bind to the split-policy plan hash and the dataset manifest hash. No gate, threshold or output contract was weakened. These receipts clear SFT for openui_verified_train_v2 only; the upstream fixes to openui_verified_v1 remain open against that corpus's own feedback artifact.

actions.note: Found by running the loop, not by reading the corpus. Admission applied a narrower output contract than the trainer, so records placing a placeholder in a non-content property (for example ':slot_0' in RadialChart.labels) reached the train bucket and made it untrainable. Admission now calls assert_role_safe_output under the same document output kind the trainer resolves, and refuses the record at a new role_safety stage; 49 refusals across the three splits are recorded in rejected.jsonl, 29 of them from the train bucket. Re-measured after the rebuild: 0 of 1,054 admitted records fail the trainer's contract. The contract was made stricter at admission, never relaxed. Re-certifying openui_verified_v1 so a placeholder only ever occupies a content property stays open against that corpus.
